paper.title: Copeland Dueling Bandit Problem: Regret Lower Bound, Optimal Algorithm, and Computationally Efficient Algorithm

unmapped: Winner notion is Copeland winner (arm beating the most other arms); Copeland winners may be non-unique
Regret per round r_{i,j} = (L_i + L_j - 2 L_1)/(2(K-1)) where L_i is number of arms beating arm i
Assumes mu_{i,j} != 1/2 for all i != j
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t=1,2,\dots,T$, the forecaster draws a pair of arms $p(t) = (l(t), m(t)) \in [K]^2$ and, receives relative feedback $\myX{l(t)}{m(t)}(t) \sim \Bernoulli(\muij{l(t)}{m(t)})$ ... We define the regret per round is $\reg{i}{j} := (\Li{i} + \Li{j} - 2 \Li{1}) / (2(K-1)) \le 1$ ... and the regret as $ \Regret(T) := \sum_{t \in [T]} \reg{l(t)}{m(t)}$.

algorithms.name: CW-RMED (Copeland Winners Relative Minimum Empirical Divergence)

symbols.C_star: min over Copeland winners i_1 of C*_{i_1}({mu_ij}), the value of the LP minimizing regret-weighted exploration subject to KL-weighted constraints for certifying i_1 as Copeland winner

conditions: strongly consistent: E[R(T)] = o(T^a) for all a>0 on every preference matrix

source.label: thm_regretlower
source.quote: The regret of a strongly consistent algorithm is lower bounded as: \Expect[\Regret(T)]\ge \min_{i_1 \in \winners} \optcone{i_1}(\{\muij{i}{j}\}) \log{T}-\so(\log T).

results.notes: Regret defined via Copeland numbers (deterministic per-pair regret), treated as pseudo-regret. Comparator is Copeland winner pair.

symbols.C_star: min over Copeland winners i_1 of C*_{i_1}({mu_ij}) (optimal LP value from the lower bound)

conditions: argmin over Copeland winners of C*_{i_1} is unique
optimal solution set R*_{i_1} is unique for each Copeland winner i_1

source.label: thm_opt
source.quote: Assume that $\argmin_{i_1 \in \winners} \optcone{i_1}(\{\muij{i}{j}\})$ and $\optset{i_1}{\{\muij{i}{j}\}}$ for each $i_1 \in \winners$ are unique. For any $\algalpha > 0$, $\algbeta>0$, the regret of CW-RMED is bounded as: \Expect[\Regret(T)]\le \min_{i_1 \in \winners} \optcone{i_1}(\{\muij{i}{j}\}) \log T +\so(\log T).

results.notes: Asymptotically optimal, matching Theorem 2. Paper argues LP solvable in polynomial time via ellipsoid method but says efficiency of naive implementation is prohibitive; compute left not_stated.

symbols.C_E: min over Copeland winners i_1 of C^{E*}_{i_1}({mu_ij}), value of the relaxed (ECW) LP; C_E >= C_star with equality when there are >= 2 Copeland winners (Theorem 6)

conditions: argmin over Copeland winners of C^{E*}_{i_1} is unique
optimal solution set R^{E*}_{i_1} is unique for each Copeland winner i_1

source.label: thm_relax
source.quote: Assume that $\argmin_{i_1 \in \winners} \optconerelax{i}(\{\muij{i}{j}\})$ and $\optsetrelax{i_1}{\{\muij{i}{j}\}}$ for each $i_1 \in \winners$ are unique. For any $\algalpha > 0$, $\algbeta>0$, the regret of ECW-RMED is bounded as: \Expect[\Regret(T)]\le \min_{i_1 \in \winners} \optconerelax{i_1}(\{\muij{i}{j}\}) \log T +\so(\log T).

results.notes: Theorem 6 shows C_E >= C_star always and C_E = C_star when the number of Copeland winners >= 2, so ECW-RMED is asymptotically optimal then. Paper also (informally) bounds C_E <= K/kl(1/2+Delta,1/2)*((L_1+3)/2 + L_1^2/K) with Delta = min |mu_ij - 1/2|.

cited_results.setting_description: K-armed Copeland dueling bandit; C = number of Copeland winners, L_1 = number of arms beating a Copeland winner, Delta = min |mu_ij - 1/2|
